decommissioning_sweep.closure: the class is closed on this host: no consumed-holdout material remains solely on EBS, and nothing is unclassified.
decommissioning_sweep.implemented_as: a classifier, not prose — the same principle as gate 11. It walks the host, hashes every candidate as bytes, and classifies by evidence-linked identity first and path rules second.
decommissioning_sweep.refuses_to_guess: UNKNOWN is a real verdict. Anything the classifier cannot place is reported as NEEDS_RULING rather than folded into a benign bucket — a classifier that cannot say 'I do not know' will silently misclassify the one file that matters.
decommissioning_sweep.scope_note: the sweep covered /opt/mr002, /root, /home, /var/tmp, /tmp, /mnt and /data, and .duckdb/.parquet/.db/.sqlite/.arrow/.feather. It is a host sweep, not a claim about any other machine.
decommissioning_sweep.standing_rule: before terminating an MR-002 host, enumerate all local DuckDB / parquet / materialization artifacts and classify each as development, fixture, failed-pre-read evidence, or consumed-holdout evidence. No consumed-holdout material may remain solely on EBS.

immutability_finding.asymmetry_worth_recording: the Validation-1 cycle protected its materialization with chattr +i; the Validation-2 cycle did NOT — the V2 database deleted without resistance. Not actionable now, since V2 is consumed and archived, but the next method version should apply the protection consistently rather than by accident of which cycle happened to set it.
immutability_finding.handled: the attribute was cleared with `chattr -i` as a recorded governance act, the hash was RE-COMPUTED in the resulting mutable window and required to equal the archived custody bytes before deletion proceeded, and the script was written to restore `chattr +i` and abort had the hash differed.
immutability_finding.observed: the first deletion attempt failed with EPERM. The file carried the ext/xfs IMMUTABLE attribute (lsattr `----i----------------`), set during the 2026-08-19 run to protect the materialized holdout.
immutability_finding.why_the_re_hash_earns_its_place: clearing immutability makes the file mutable for a window. The re-hash between clearing and deleting is the only thing that proves the bytes deleted are the bytes archived.

prefix_naming_decision.date_component_convention: the date is the MATERIALIZATION date, not the transfer date. For V2 those coincided (2026-08-21); for V1 they do not, so the convention is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a single example.
prefix_naming_decision.why: the V2 object's location is now evidentiary identity and cannot move. A second naming scheme for a class of exactly two members would leave the generations under different conventions — the same split that has produced six role-transfer defects in this program. Symmetry with the immovable member beats tidiness that only half the class can adopt.

/opt/mr002/stage/v2open/run/validation2..why: zero tables, zero Validation-2 content, and it is the artifact behind the PreReadFailure record's claim. Owner-ruled RETAIN. It does not create the consumed-corpus reuse risk.

step_2_write_via_the_hosts_only_sanction.independent_agreement: S3 computed the digest itself at write time and it equals the host's — two independent computations, not one repeated

The bytes sat there only between the write and the promotion, and the staging version was then deleted. This window is structural: the host's IAM policy permits PutObject to that prefix and nowhere else, and widening it would mean editing the latch document. It is disclosed rather than hidden.
